subject: Buffer overflow in featureCounts with large "extra" tags

messages.author: c474545bb380efaf
messages.subject: Buffer overflow in featureCounts with large "extra" tags
parts:
Hi,

Recent versions of BWA sometimes emit very long XA tags for multimapping alignments. These tags can overflow the statically allocated extra_tags buffer in sambam-file.c, leading to a crash.

The attached tarball includes a realistic minimal reproduction of the problem; the SAM header is representative of that emitted by BWA 0.7.15 when aligning to GRCh38 with alt contigs and decoys, and the first read is telomeric sequence with a multi-kb XA tag. Note that this read is real data that came off a sequencer and was emitted by BWA; it is not an artificial test case.

The attached patch files (also included in the tarball) mitigate the overflow and come in two parts:
  • a patch to core.h statically increases the size of the extra_tags buffer from 400 bytes to 4KB
  • a patch to sambam-file.c checks for buffer overrun at each sprintf/memcpy into extra tags, and crashes if an overrun is detected
With neither patch applied, subread-1.5.1 will crash (either segfault or trigger the runtime stack smashing protector) on the given test case. With only the sambam-file.c patch applied, it will detect the overflow at runtime, exit, and indicate where the problem occurred. With both patches applied, the test case runs.

There appear to be a number of other arrays where a similar problem could occur (statically allocated buffers) and at least one existing similar mitigation at sambam-file.c line 594. It would probably be better to use dynamically allocated buffers in this code, but the diversity of exit points makes it difficult to retrofit onto the existing function.

Hopefully this patch can be incorporated into the next minor revision of subread.

Thanks,

Imran
